critical.title: Vault TLS completely disabled in production configuration
critical.impact: All Vault traffic (including root tokens, encryption keys, biometric data encryption keys) transmitted in cleartext on network. VAULT_ADDR set to https:// but TLS disabled - creates false sense of security.
critical.production_risk: CRITICAL - Secrets exposed on container network; if network compromised, all secrets leaked

critical.title: secrets/ directory not in .gitignore - real secrets committed risk
critical.evidence: .gitignore lacks 'secrets/' entry; git status shows secrets/ as untracked
critical.impact: Generated production passwords (postgres, redis, vault_token, grafana) and placeholder API keys could be accidentally committed. Currently: postgres_password, redis_password, vault_token, grafana_password are REAL generated values.
critical.production_risk: HIGH - If committed, all production credentials leaked to git history

critical.title: Vault running in dev mode with static root token in docker-compose.yaml
critical.impact: Dev mode uses in-memory storage, no seal/unseal, static root token 'root'. This pattern could leak to prod if compose files confused.
critical.production_risk: MEDIUM - Dev workaround that should never reach production

high.title: Both vault-tls/ and nginx-tls/ directories are empty
high.evidence: ls -la shows both directories exist but contain zero certificate files
high.impact: docker-compose.prod.yaml mounts ./config/vault-tls:/vault/tls:ro and ./config/nginx-tls:/etc/nginx/tls:ro - containers will fail to start or fail TLS handshake. Vault healthcheck uses -tls-skip-verify masking the issue.
high.production_risk: HIGH - Production deployment will fail or run without TLS despite https:// config

high.title: PostgreSQL port 5432 exposed to host in production
high.impact: Database directly accessible from host network. Should only be accessible within docker network.
high.production_risk: HIGH - Unnecessary attack surface; credentials in env vars but network exposure remains

high.title: Redis port 6379 exposed to host in production
high.impact: Redis directly accessible from host. Password protected but unnecessary exposure.

high.title: Vault ports 8200/8201 exposed to host in production
high.impact: Vault API and cluster ports exposed to host. Combined with tls_disable=true, this is severe.
high.production_risk: CRITICAL - Vault API exposed without TLS to host network

high.title: Monitoring stack ports exposed to host (9091, 3001, 9093)
high.impact: Prometheus, Grafana, Alertmanager accessible from host. Grafana has file-based password but no IP restriction.
high.production_risk: MEDIUM - Monitoring interfaces should be behind VPN/auth proxy

high.title: API ports 3000 and 9090 exposed to host directly
high.impact: API bypasses nginx TLS termination and rate limiting. Metrics endpoint (9090) exposed.
high.production_risk: HIGH - Bypasses all nginx security controls (rate limiting, auth, TLS)

medium.title: nginx CSP allows unsafe-inline and unsafe-eval for scripts
medium.impact: Weakens XSS protection. Should use nonces or hashes instead.

medium.title: Vault audit log mode 0644 - readable by all container users
medium.impact: Audit logs may contain sensitive access patterns. Should be 0600 or 0640.
medium.production_risk: LOW-MEDIUM - Information leakage in shared container environments

medium.title: Vault UI enabled in production (ui = true)
medium.impact: Web UI exposes additional attack surface. Should be disabled in production unless explicitly needed.

medium.title: setup-secrets.sh recommends chmod 600 but doesn't enforce it
medium.evidence: scripts/setup-secrets.sh lines 108-110: suggests chmod 600 but doesn't execute it
medium.impact: Secret files remain world-readable (644) by default. In container, mounted as root but host perms matter.

medium.title: Grafana hardcoded admin username 'admin'
medium.impact: Predictable username for admin account. Should be randomized or configurable.
medium.production_risk: LOW - Password is secret but username is known

low.title: Application uses postgres superuser account
low.impact: Application has full DB privileges. Should use least-privilege role.
low.production_risk: LOW - Standard practice but not least privilege

low.title: disable_mlock = false but IPC_LOOK cap added - inconsistent
low.evidence: config/vault.hcl line 33: disable_mlock = false; docker-compose.prod.yaml line 66: cap_add: IPC_LOCK
low.impact: mlock requires IPC_LOCK capability. Config says don't disable mlock but doesn't guarantee it works in all container runtimes.
low.production_risk: LOW - Memory paging possible if mlock fails silently

contradictions.description: VAULT_ADDR set to https:// but tls_disable = true in vault.hcl
docker-compose.prod.yaml mounts vault-tls/ and nginx-tls/ as :ro but directories are empty
Production compose uses secrets/ files but .gitignore doesn't exclude secrets/
API service exposes ports 3000/9090 directly AND nginx proxies to api:3000 - duplicate exposure
Vault healthcheck uses -tls-skip-verify masking missing TLS certs

required_conditions: Vault MUST have TLS enabled (tls_disable = false) with valid certificates in vault-tls/ before production deployment
nginx-tls/ MUST contain valid fullchain.pem and privkey.pem before production deployment
secrets/ MUST be added to .gitignore immediately
PostgreSQL, Redis, Vault, and monitoring ports should NOT be exposed to host in production - use internal docker network only
API ports 3000/9090 should NOT be exposed to host - all traffic must go through nginx
Vault should NOT run in dev mode (docker-compose.yaml pattern must not leak to prod)
CSP should use nonces/hashes instead of unsafe-inline/unsafe-eval
Vault audit log mode should be 0600 or 0640
Vault UI should be disabled (ui = false) in production
setup-secrets.sh should enforce chmod 600 on generated secret files
Grafana admin username should be configurable, not hardcoded 'admin'
risks_unknowns: Whether self-signed certs for local Vault HTTPS verification would weaken production posture: YES - if self-signed certs are used in production, clients must disable verification or trust custom CA, creating habit of skipping verification. Better: use proper CA (Let's Encrypt, internal PKI) for both local and prod, or use TLS termination at load balancer with valid certs.

Empty cert directories cause silent failures: Vault healthcheck passes due to -tls-skip-verify, nginx will fail to start or serve on port 443. Production deployment will appear healthy but TLS not working.
Dev compose has VAULT_ADDR=http:// (no TLS) while prod has VAULT_ADDR=https:// but TLS disabled - inconsistent config patterns between dev/prod increase misconfiguration risk.
API keys for ElevenLabs, Veo, Runway, Luma are placeholders - deployment will fail at runtime if not replaced.
No evidence of secret rotation strategy - vault_token is static, postgres/redis passwords static.
No network policies or firewall rules defined - all containers on same bridge network with full connectivity.
Alertmanager webhook URL is placeholder - alerting will not work.
Archive backend config (S3) credentials not in secrets - ARCHIVE_BUCKET env var but no AWS credentials in compose.
